subject: Quantapay: production payment failures and latency spike - closure & commitments
messages:
From: Tomasz Kowalski <tomasz@quantapay.com>

Cc: Quantapay Support <support@quantapay.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@quantapay.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2026 10:22:00 -0400
Subject: urgent: payment authorization failures and 2-3s spikes in tokenization latency

Kimberly / Redwood team,

We're seeing recurring failures in payment authorizations between 09:40 and 10:05 UTC this morning. ~4% of requests are returning 5xx from your tokenization endpoint and many of the successful ones saw latency increase from our baseline 120ms to 2-3s. This has directly caused ~150 failed payment attempts in production and a spike in support tickets.

Can you confirm you've seen this? We need an immediate triage update and timeline for mitigation. Our merchants are already experiencing chargebacks.

I've included Elena (ops) and our support alias. Please escalate to whoever owns SLA/credits — we will expect a follow-up on whether this qualifies for service credit under our contract.

Thanks,
Tomasz
Head of Platform, QuantaPay
T: +44 20 7946 0218

Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2026 11:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: urgent: payment authorization failures and 2-3s spikes in tokenization latency

On Mon, Mar 8, 2026 at 11:02 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Tomasz — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the impact. I've opened INC-4821...

Quick summary from infra triage: around 09:37 UTC we saw a sustained increase in concurrent requests for the tokenization route (+220% above baseline) that caused backpressure on the KV cache maintenance daemon. That daemon serialized several large cache compactions which blocked worker threads for short windows (1-3s) and triggered request timeouts upstream.

Mitigation performed (11:00 UTC):
- Disabled background compaction on the affected pool (hotfix)
- Temporarily increased worker thread count for the tokenization service
- Added a traffic routing rule to spill overflow to a warm fallback cluster

We've captured the request traces and are compiling a timeline. Attaching draft timeline and resource spike graph.

Attachments: quantapay-incident-timeline.pdf

Marcus
Senior On-call Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Tomasz Kowalski <tomasz@quantapay.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@quantapay.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2026 12:10:00 -04:00
Subject: RE: urgent: payment authorization failures and 2-3s spikes in tokenization latency — initial impact and next steps

Tomasz / Elena —

Thank you for the example request id (included below). Marcus's team has applied the mitigations described and we have seen error rate drop back to baseline (0.2%) and median latency return to ~140ms as of 11:05 UTC.

What we will deliver by EOD tomorrow:
- A full incident timeline (attached) with trace ids and root-cause narrative (quantapay-incident-timeline.pdf)
- A set of short-term mitigations we will keep in place for the next 72 hours
- A proposed schedule for durable fixes (KV cache compaction refactor + smarter compaction windowing) with estimated ETA (2–3 weeks) and rollback/fallback runbook

On the SLA/credits question — we will review the contract and internal precedents; I have looped in Vivek and Jonas for executive sign-off on any customer credit.

Request for you: please confirm a primary contact for post-incident calls and whether QuantaPay prefers a public readout or a private technical review.

Best,
Kim

Subject: Quantapay escalation closure — commitments for fix schedule, runbook, and credit proposal

Team —

Summary / recommended customer commitments (for sign-off):
1) Draft technical post-incident report delivered to customer (attached) — sent 2026-03-08 12:10 UTC.
2) Short-term controls to remain for 72 hours (disabled compaction, increased workers, routing rule).
3) Durable fix: refactor KV compaction to non-blocking windowed compaction + safety throttle; ETA 3 weeks (target 2026-03-29).
4) Runbook additions: automated detection of compaction backpressure and automatic spill-to-fallback (in next sprint).
5) Credit proposal: 5% of one monthly invoice for the incident window (calculation attached in qpay-mitigation-commitments.csv).

I recommend we offer the 5% credit pending legal sign-off and record the fix ETA in the Dedicated customer's rollout calendar. Vivek/Jonas — please confirm approval for the credit and let me know if you want a lower/higher offer for exec alignment.

Once approved I will:
- Send the credit proposal and timeline to Elena/Tomasz and schedule the private technical review (this week).
- Create follow-up Jira (INC-4821 -> INC-4821-FIX) and assign owners.

Thanks — Kim

Vivek's quick reply: APPROVED (on thread). Jonas: please respond with any caveats.
